slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The provided code snippet is a large, heavily minified and transpiled JavaScript bundle that primarily implements asynchronous generator functions, promise handling, and utility functions for iteration and class inheritance. It includes a Sentry debug ID injection for error tracking and references to SDK event names, indicating it is part of a legitimate SDK or library. There is no evidence of dynamic script injection, obfuscated external network calls, or attempts to load remote scripts from attacker-controlled domains as seen in the known malicious patterns. The code does not perform suspicious operations such as creating script tags with external URLs, nor does it obfuscate standard library calls to evade detection. The behavior summary indicates XMLHttpRequest usage for asynchronous HTTP communication, which is common and not inherently malicious. Compared to the known malicious patterns, which involve dynamic script injection from suspicious domains or obfuscation to hide filesystem access, this code lacks those indicators. Therefore, it is likely benign.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the injected code appends a script tag with src set to https://send.wagateway.pro/client.js?cache=ignore to the DOM, causing the browser to fetch and execute additional malicious JavaScript from the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated and mass-injected into all JavaScript files, ensuring that every page load triggers the download and execution of untrusted code from an external domain controlled by the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not inject remote scripts from unrelated or untrusted domains into all JavaScript files, especially using obfuscation and without user or developer consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is sometimes used for analytics or feature toggles, but not in an obfuscated, repository-wide, and externally controlled manner.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript injected into all *.js files
Dynamically creates a script tag with src pointing to send.wagateway.pro/client.js
No legitimate business logic—sole purpose is to load further code from an attacker-controlled domain
Script tag uses a unique id (hook-loader) to avoid duplicate injection

execution_context.trigger: At runtime in the browser when any modified JavaScript file is loaded
execution_context.file_location: assets/js/*.js (appended to the end of every JavaScript file in the repository)

package_info.why_malicious: The attack involves unauthorized commits impersonating Dependabot, introducing a malicious GitHub Actions workflow and modifying all JavaScript files to exfiltrate repository secrets and end-user credentials. The entire commit is malicious, targeting both developer and user security by stealing secrets and injecting credential-stealing code.

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains a developer's GitHub personal access token (PAT), likely via a separate malicious package or phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to authenticate as the victim and push code to their repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the stolen PAT to commit malicious code to the victim's repositories, impersonating Dependabot to avoid suspicion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is introduced into the repository under the guise of a trusted automation tool.

attack_chain.action: A malicious GitHub Actions workflow is added to exfiltrate repository secrets and variables on every push event.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository secrets and variables are sent to the attacker's command and control (C2) server.

attack_chain.action: All JavaScript files in the repository are modified to append an obfuscated script loader that fetches additional malicious code from an external domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-users of the web application are exposed to further malicious payloads when they load the compromised JavaScript files.

attack_chain.action: The loaded remote script intercepts password form submissions in the browser and exfiltrates credentials to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-user credentials are stolen and sent to the attacker's C2 server, achieving the attacker's final objective.

Flag any network traffic to send.wagateway.pro domains as a high-confidence indicator of compromise.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At import-time, the code defines obfuscated helper functions to dynamically access Node.js filesystem methods (readdirSync, existsSync, readFileSync), enabling stealthy file system access and evasion of static analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscating method names for standard library functions is a common tactic to evade static analysis and hide malicious intent, making it harder for defenders to detect file system access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate access to core Node.js modules or dynamically construct method names for standard APIs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used in proprietary code to protect intellectual property, but not in open-source utility libraries where transparency is expected.

Obfuscation of standard library access
Helper functions that mask real API calls

package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate 'chalk' package, published by an impersonated author account. It contains obfuscated code in 'index.esm.js' that, at import-time, initializes a Sentry SDK with a hardcoded DSN, accesses the user's filesystem, reads potentially sensitive files, intercepts console output, and exfiltrates this data to an external Sentry instance without user consent. The package copies the README and structure of the real 'chalk' package to deceive users and compromise their data.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious 'chalk-node' package, triggering execution of index.esm.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sentry is initialized with a hardcoded DSN and obfuscated file system access helpers are set up, preparing the environment for data exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Whenever console.log is called, the overridden function reads files from a '../data' directory and checks log arguments for sensitive patterns.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive file contents and log data are prepared for exfiltration to the attacker's Sentry instance.

attack_chain.action: File contents and/or log data are sent to the attacker's Sentry instance, using chunked messages and obfuscated prefixes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated data; user remains unaware due to silent error handling and obfuscated code.
